title: Isometric invariance of correlated Gaussian measure
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $Q$ be a linear isometry of Euclidean $\mathbb R^n$. The joint law of a standard Gaussian vector and its coordinatewise $\rho$-correlated Gaussian partner is unchanged when $Q$ is applied to both vectors.
hypotheses_covered: $Q$ is a linear isometry of Euclidean $\mathbb R^n$
